properties.name: WHAT WORKED (field log 2026-10-01 on 0.76.0, re-measured 2026-10-05 on 0.76.0 and main): while a --serve-shared server holds a design, a --call read answers from a snapshot with a loud stderr warning, a --call write is refused naming why and writes nothing, and --stop-shared releases the design. Do not regress it. On 0.76.0 the snapshot's search answered nothing, which 0.78.0 fixed
properties.statement:
Field log [works], 2026-10-01 (art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05): "Held graph: a read on a store held by a Claude Code --serve-shared daemon answered from a best-effort snapshot with a loud stderr warning; a write was refused with a clear message, nothing written. --stop-shared then released it cleanly."

RE-MEASURED, scratch store holding one requirement that says "zebra pattern", a --serve-shared server holding it:
- 0.76.0: the read printed "reflow2: WARNING — BEST-EFFORT SNAPSHOT …" on stderr. search_design for "zebra pattern" returned 0 hits, the false empty root-caused in fact:root-cause-a-held-design-answers-search-through-the-door-with-a-false-nothing-matched-2026-10-02. The write was refused: "`add_requirement` writes, so it needs the graph itself and not a snapshot copy … another process already has the design graph", exit 1. --stop-shared: "asked the shared server … to stop". Afterwards the refused requirement was absent.
- main: the same warning, and search_design returned 1 hit (#657 in 0.78.0). The write refusal and --stop-shared behave as on 0.76.0.

So the praise holds for the write refusal and the release. For reads, it holds from 0.78.0 on.
